executive_summary: Architectural placement analysis identifies that `ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/tests/step-3-evaluation.json` serves as the consolidated single source of truth for both the evaluation method heuristic and the complete Step3_TSR question corpus (Tests 2–32, 97 total cases). In the active architecture, it replaces `ChatMachines/GeminiSupervisor/evaluation-tests.md` and historical markdown-based references. In `Agents.md`, references in Step 3 field definitions, evaluation requirements, and supervisory gate instructions should point directly to this JSON artifact locator. In `send-to-gemini.js`, the runner should replace `testsPath` with `step3EvaluationPath`, load the JSON artifact as a unified object, inject it into the Step 3 execution and supervisory prompts/system context, and optionally use its structured `tests` array to dynamically validate `Test_Count` and test results. Loading the heuristic and TSR corpus together as a single parsed JSON object avoids dual-file I/O, prevents drift between the comparator method and test cases, and ensures complete traceability.

requirement_evaluations.explanation: Recommendation: Load together as a unified object. `step-3-evaluation.json` was deliberately constructed with two top-level keys: `evaluation_heuristic` (the U/P comparator method) and `step3_tsr` (the test suite). Splitting them at runtime introduces unnecessary file handles and potential synchronization drift. Loading the merged JSON once into memory at runtime and passing it as unified structured context to Gemini Step 3 execution and supervisory gates ensures the model sees both the decision heuristic and the specific questions simultaneously.
